children.text: tvaṃ bhūmim iti pavitre'ntardhāya havirnirvapati devasya tvā iti
children.translated_text: Having interposed the purifiers, he offers the <s>havis</s> with the mantra, "You are the earth..." and "Of the god, you..."

children.text: tvaṃ bhūmim iti kalpajayā pavitre carmaṇaḥ vrīhīṇāṃ cāntarā kṛtvā haviścarmaṇi karoti devasya tvā ityanena mantreṇa
children.translated_text: With the formula "You are the earth," according to the ritual rule, after placing the purifiers between the hide and the rice grains, he puts the <s>havis</s> on the hide with the mantra "Of the god, you..."
Since the action is understood from the mantra itself, the mention of offering is an explicit injunction.

children.text: nirvāpe mantrābhāvāt kriyā na syāt tadarthaṃ mantrasiddhamapi nirvapatigrahaṇaṃ punarucyate
children.translated_text: Because, in the act of offering, if there were no mantra the action would not occur, the mention of offering is stated again for that purpose, even though it is established by the mantra.
With the right hand, three handfuls.
Silently, a fourth.
The word <s>havis</s> is used so that this should not apply to eatable <s>sthālīpāka</s> offerings.
In connection with proximity we shall state the distinctions.

children.text: caturvidhāḥ sthālīpākāḥ vyaktacodanāḥ avyaktacodanāḥ vyaktāvyaktacodanā āśyāśceti
children.translated_text: The <s>sthālīpākas</s> are of four kinds: those with an explicit injunction, those with an implicit injunction, those with both explicit and implicit injunction, and those that are eatable.
One sacrifices to <s>Indra</s> with a <s>puroḍāśa</s>.
And this sacrifice is for the rites of return from studentship and completion.

children.text: idaṃ tad yuje yat kiṃcāsau manasetyāhitāgniṃ pratinirvapati samāvṛtyāśnāti udāharaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: "This is that yoke, whatever he, with his mind..." He offers it in regard to one who has established the sacred fires; having returned, he eats it. These are examples.
Likewise with the phrase "for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>."
In the offering-mantra, "for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>" is a portion of the mantra.
The offering is for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: evamiti pavitrāntardhānāditi prāpte'rthe agnaye ityasya sthāne agnīṣomābhyām iti viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the matter has been reached by "likewise," beginning with the interposition of the purifiers, the special point is that "for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>" stands in place of "for <s>Agni</s>."
"For <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>" is used at the new moon.
Likewise at the new moon, even where the injunction is implicit, the offering beginning with the interposition of the purifiers is to be performed.
But the special form is: "I offer what is pleasing to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>."
The mention of the new moon would be purposeless.
For "at the non-appearance, for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>" would already have the connection with the new moon.
Because it is already established.
It is not purposeless.

children.text: nityaṃ pūrvamāgneyam ityatra nityagrahaṇaṃ sahāvahanane'pyāgneyasya parvāṇi pūrvatvāt
children.translated_text: In the statement "the <s>āgneya</s> is always first," the word "always" is used because the <s>āgneya</s> has priority on the lunar day even when the carrying together has been done.
And from that there would arise an option between the offering for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> and the one for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
To prevent that, the statement "at the new moon" is made.
The <s>āgneya</s> is always first.
And at all times the prescription of the <s>āgneya</s> offering is to be understood first.

children.text: sahāvahanane kṛte vibhajyamāneṣu ye taṇḍulāḥ prathamaṃ vibhaktāste āgneyā iti
children.translated_text: When the carrying together has been done and the rice grains are being divided, those divided first are the <s>āgneya</s> grains.
And after the pounding, the priority of the <s>āgneya</s> is not useless.

children.text: niruptaṃ pavitrābhyāṃ prokṣatyamuṣmai tvā juṣṭamiti yathādevatam
children.translated_text: He sprinkles what has been offered with the two purifiers, saying, "For so-and-so, you are pleasing," according to the deity.
He sprinkles with the two purifiers the rice grains that are on the hide.
For whichever deity the rice grains have been offered,
he sprinkles them.

children.text: agnaye tvā juṣṭaṃ prokṣāmīti agnīṣomābhyāṃ tvā juṣṭaṃ prokṣāmīti nidarśanam
children.translated_text: "For <s>Agni</s>, I sprinkle you as pleasing," and "For <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, I sprinkle you as pleasing" are examples.
In cases with an implicit injunction it is without a mantra, because the word "offered" is used.
In the offering-mantra, according to the prescription, the understanding is like that of the hand-washing mantra.

children.text: ulūkhalamusalaṃ śūrpaṃ prakṣālitaṃ carmaṇyādhāya vrīhīnulūkhala opyāvaghnaṃs trir haviṣkṛtā vācaṃ visṛjati haviṣkṛd ā dravehīti
children.translated_text: Having washed the mortar, pestle, and winnowing basket, placed them on the hide, poured the rice grains into the mortar, and pounded them, he releases the speech of the maker of the <s>havis</s> three times: "Maker of the <s>havis</s>, come running here."
He should wash the mortar and pestle, and also the winnowing basket.
This is what is stated in the mantra beginning "Whatever is black..."
He should set the washed implements on the hide used for the offering.
The sacrificer throws the offered rice grains into the mortar and pounds them.

children.text: avaghnaṃśca haviṣkṛtā mantreṇa haviṣkṛd ā dravehīti triḥ vācaṃ visṛjati
children.translated_text: And while pounding, with the mantra of the maker of the <s>havis</s>, "Maker of the <s>havis</s>, come running here," he releases his speech three times.
Because the meaning is expressed.
He washes with the mantra "What of you is spotted..."
This is what is stated in the mantra "Whatever is black..."
Thus the washing of the mortar and the other implements takes place.
"Washed" means the substance has been ritually prepared.
In explicitly enjoined cases there is an indication of a particular meaning.
The statement "having placed it on the hide" is made because the preparation of the <s>havis</s> on the hide is connected with the prescribed rite.
The word "rice grains" is for the understanding that the <s>havis</s> is involved in the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices.
The mention of offering, because it serves to establish all <s>havis</s> offerings, is for such things as sesame seeds and the like.

children.text: paścādagnervāgyataḥ saṃviśati ityata ārabhya vāgyamo vitānavat
children.translated_text: Beginning from "he sits down behind the fire, restraining speech," the restraint of speech is as in the extended rite.
"Maker of the <s>havis</s>, come here" is said because he is the agent in preparing the <s>havis</s>.
The word "preparation of the <s>havis</s>" refers to placing it on the purifiers.
The pounding belongs to the maker of the <s>havis</s>.
And this follows from the later phrase "having pounded," because the same agent is indicated.

children.text: avadṛtya suphalīkṛtān kṛtvā triḥ prakṣālya taṇḍulān agne caruryajñiyastvādhyarukṣat iti carumadhidadhāti
children.translated_text: Having removed it, made the rice well cleaned from husk and chaff, and washed the grains three times, he places the <s>caru</s> on the fire with the mantra, "O <s>Agni</s>, the sacrificial <s>caru</s> has mounted upon you."
After pounding, until the production of the rice grains is complete.
Having made them very thoroughly separated from the husks.
The husk-removals are the husks and chaff.

children.text: prakṣālyodakena taṇḍulān agne carurityagnau caruṃ sthāpayati
children.translated_text: Having washed the rice grains with water, with "O <s>Agni</s>, the <s>caru</s>..." he places the <s>caru</s> on the fire.
The word <s>caru</s> is used so that this should not apply to the new potsherds and cups.
The words belonging to each <s>havis</s> are not combined, because they occur together.
With "pure, purified," he pours in water.
With this verse he pours it in.
He interposes the purifiers, by extension from the context.
Together with the mantra, the moistening of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> takes place.
The word "water" is used so that milk should not be meant.
With "purified by <s>Brahman</s>," he treats the rice grains.
Immediately after the sprinkling of water, he puts in the rice grains.
The word "rice grains" is used so that sesame porridge should not be meant.
Because in all cases there is a different time, the word "puts in" is used.
The waters; in them are the rice grains.

children.text: pari tvāgne puraṃ vayam iti triḥparyagni karoti
children.translated_text: With "Around you, O <s>Agni</s>, we make a fortress," he makes the fire pass around three times.
With this verse he carries fire around the <s>caru</s> three times.
But the mantra is recited once, since there is one substance.
The mention of "three times" is for avoiding a minimum of three being left uncertain.
With the inspection, he lifts it up clockwise three times.
The upward striking, with the face turned toward it, is the winnowing upward of the rice-grains.
He stirs the <s>caru</s>.
The striking is not done with looking on.
The statement about moving clockwise is for the sake of regulating the action as desired.
From this point onward, it is as desired.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ āghaṭṭanamanāghaṭṭanaṃ vā pradakṣiṇamapradakṣiṇaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Thereafter, there may be striking or no striking, and it may be clockwise or not clockwise.
He places the fuel to the north of the fire.
Having brought the fuel near, he places it there.
The barhis is to the north.
It is to the north of the fuel.
With 'For <s>Agni</s>, I sprinkle you, acceptable,' he sprinkles the fuel.
'He sprinkles' is the remainder of the sentence.
This follows from the statement, 'Thus the ritual acts are indicated by marks.'
With 'Of the earth,' he sprinkles the barhis.

children.text: pṛthivyai tvā juṣṭaṃ prokṣāmīti barhiḥ prokṣati
children.translated_text: With 'For the earth I sprinkle you, acceptable,' he sprinkles the barhis.
Since both the fuel and the barhis have been placed, the mention of the fuel and barhis is for the sake of sprinkling them.
'Of the earth' is the utterance of the complete mantra.
Because it has already been obtained from the governing rule.
So too in the case of 'For <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>,' and the like.

children.text: darbhamuṣṭimabhyukṣya paścādagneḥ prāgagraṃ nidadhātyūrṇamradaṃ prathasva svāsasthaṃ devebhya iti
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled a handful of darbha, he places it behind the fire with its tips toward the east, saying, 'Spread out as wool-soft, well-seated for the gods.'

children.text: yo muṣṭiḥ prathamo lūnas taṃ paścādagneḥ pūrvāgraṃ nidadhāti
children.translated_text: The handful that was cut first he places behind the fire with its tips eastward.
Because the injunction has ceased, there is a separate statement about the first handful at the time of cutting.
Because at the time of cutting the statement here requires that it certainly be taken.
In the <s>ājya</s>-procedure, since sufficiency is present, it is not taken again.

children.text: darbhāṇāmapādāya ṛṣīṇāṃ prastaro'si iti dakṣiṇato'gnerbrahmāsanaṃ nidadhāti
children.translated_text: Taking some darbha, with 'You are the strewn seat of the seers,' he places the Brahmā's seat to the south of the fire.

children.text: darbhebhyaḥ paribhojanīyebhyaḥ apādāya darbhān pradakṣiṇamagnervedyāmeva vediryajñasya iti vacanāt
children.translated_text: Taking darbha from the darbhas meant for surrounding use, he moves clockwise around the fire, on the altar itself, because of the statement, 'The altar is the sacrifice.'
The seat of the Brahmā is the Brahmā-seat.
Here the choosing of the Brahmā is as in the <s>Vitāna</s>.
There is also the muttering after being chosen.
Because of the <s>Vitāna</s> statement, 'Having been chosen, he mutters.'
It is 'I am the lord of the earth,' and so on.

children.text: purastādagnerāstīrya teṣāṃ mūlānyapareṣāṃ prāntairavacchādayan parisarpati dakṣiṇenāgnim ā paścārdhāt
children.translated_text: Having spread them in front of the fire, covering the roots of some with the tips of others, he goes around on the south side of the fire as far as the western half.
Beginning from the middle region of the northern altar, he spreads them.
Covering them, he goes on every side.
He goes for the purpose of spreading, on the south side of the fire, as far as the western half of the altar.
He gives the command, 'Spread around.'
The Brahmā gives the command to the performer.
The first command-statement concerns the prastara.
The command is repeated for the sake of spreading on the northern side.
Otherwise the altar would remain incomplete.
The expression 'having been commanded' would then have to be used again.
Therefore the later statement of this verse, 'Of the god, you ...,' is solely for the sake of connecting it with the side.
